events.text:
⚡️🇺🇸🇮🇷 — Secretary of State Marco Rubio told G7 counterparts in Paris on Tuesday that President Trump had weighed resuming the war with Iran or cutting a deal, but ultimately chose a third path: strangling the Iranian regime economically, according to three people who attended the meeting, cited by Axios.
➡️ After meeting Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani on Monday, Trump said a new round of strikes is "quite unlikely" and "doesn't seem to be necessary." He instead favors continuing the economic crackdown and naval blockade, alongside a new operation dubbed "Iron Gate" to cut off land routes Iran uses to move advanced weaponry and other technology.
➡️ Rubio explained the policy in the closed-door meeting: "The President doesn't just have two options. It's not just return to war or sign a ridiculous peace deal. We won't do a stupid deal. The third option we have is to continue to do what we do now." He added that the U.S. is imposing devastating costs on Iran's economy and there is no end date: "The President is not under false time pressure, the Iranians are inflicting major damage on their own economy."
➡️ U.S. officials say Rubio pushed for the "strangulation" strategy along with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, CIA Director John Ratcliffe, and Jared Kushner. That group opposed resuming war, doubted Iran's current positions could lead to an acceptable deal, and lobbied for the third option.
➡️ Rubio remains deeply skeptical of a diplomatic breakthrough: "Iran would love a deal. The problem is the conditions they continue to place are absurd. Like, they're not even serious right now." He suggested that could change with more economic pain: "Eventually you have to eat. Eventually the economic realities penetrate the skull of even the most radical lunatic."
➡️ Several U.S. allies — including Turkey, Iraq, and Pakistan — are concerned that prolonging the economic squeeze will create instability in their own countries, a U.S. official said, as Washington pressures them to stop doing business with Iran, including halting flights and closing borders.
➡️ The chosen course contradicts a directive from Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, who ordered an end to the "no war, no deal" status quo and demanded a clear conclusion to the war. If the stalemate continues and pressure intensifies, analysts warn the IRGC could see it as a green light for more aggressive regional attacks to break the status quo, risking another military confrontation neither side necessarily wants.
➡️ The Qatari prime minister briefed the G7 on mediation efforts and said he came away from his meeting with Trump believing there is more breathing room for diplomacy. Sticking points remain over which side takes the first de-escalation step, and he wants to bring in China and European countries as guarantors to ease Iranian suspicions that Trump will break any agreement.

🇪🇺🛢📉 How Europeans Will Pay for US-Israel War on Iran
Europe is approaching winter with depleted gas reserves and prices near three times their February level, leaving households and factories exposed if temperatures plunge. The US-Israeli war against Iran has disrupted supplies just as the continent needs enough fuel to cover its peak heating demand.
The European gas benchmark crossed €100 per megawatt-hour on October 28 for the first time since 2022. EU storage was only 75% full on October 21, according to EU energy regulator ACER, leaving a much thinner cushion against cold weather and interruptions to imports.
Europe’s growing reliance on liquefied natural gas, cooled for transport by ship, makes a cold spell in Asia a European problem too. Buyers compete for available cargoes, so higher Asian demand can push up the price Europe must pay even when its own weather stays mild.
ACER says no significant volumes of Qatari liquefied gas reached the EU over the summer. US supplies now account for roughly 30% of the bloc’s total gas supply, as Qatari and Russian deliveries have fallen. Reducing dependence on Russia has left Europe more exposed to American exports and competition in global shipping markets.
The cost reaches well beyond heating bills. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen says the closure of the Strait of Hormuz has added €127B to Europe’s fossil fuel import bill without buying any additional energy. Governments already carrying heavy debts face pressure to subsidize consumers while businesses absorb higher operating costs.
Bloomberg describes a 182-year-old German porcelain factory preparing to shut its kilns and Polish fertilizer producers seeking government intervention. For industries that need large amounts of heat or gas, prolonged high prices can turn a temporary production cut into a permanent closure.
Forecasts of a broadly mild winter offer some relief, but an average seasonal temperature cannot rule out damaging cold spells. A burst of heating demand would drain storage faster; simultaneous cold in Asia would make replacement cargoes more expensive.
Europe is paying for a war launched by its own allies. Subsidies can spread the bill, but they cannot replace missing gas. A severe winter would force European governments to spend more protecting households from the fallout while manufacturers face deeper cuts, closures and lost competitiveness.

👁 Anduril takes warfighting ambitions into space with new satellite surveillance tech
[Pentagon-linked](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/74041) drone [maker Anduril](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/75099) is expanding into space warfare, unveiling new technologies designed to monitor potential adversary spacecraft in orbit.
🔊 “We’re hearing clearly from the government that space is a warfighting domain,” Anduril's space division chief Gokul Subramanian told reporters, touting the new tech.
The systems were tested aboard its first satellite, ANDURIL-216, launched on a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket in July.
🔴 ANDURIL-216’s main payload is a long-wave infrared (LWIR) sensor that can detect and track spacecraft even when they are hidden in Earth's shadow
🔴 satellite also carries two additional electro-optical imaging sensors 
🔴 power-management system is designed to work with different types of satellite platforms
Anduril, flush with [Pentagon contracts](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/67181) touts the mission as being aimed at developing its ability to integrate entire satellite systems for future military projects.
However, the defense contractor’s track record raises questions about the reliability of its tech. Flaws in its NGC2 battlefield communications platform, developed with partners including [Palantir](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/74041), were flagged as “very high risk” in a recent internal US Army memo.
Anduril-powered drone boats, Altius munitions have suffered crashes [and targeting failures](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/70886), yet the Silicon Valley weapons firm continues to swoop up major Pentagon backing –[ expanding](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/75761) into new military domains.

events.text:
🇮🇱 Israel keeps clinging to Iron Beam wonder weapon despite questionable performance
Despite the fact that the Iron Beam laser defense system played little role in defensing Israel against Iran’s retaliatory strikes in 2026, Israel intends to produce more of these weapons and to integrate them further into the country’s air defenses, The Jerusalem Post reports.
🔴 The Israeli military admitted in May that it simply does not have enough Iron Beam batteries to create a significant enough impact on Iranian attacks
🔴 Ground-based Iron Beam platforms, as it turns out, simply cannot tackle ballistic missiles, and the air- and space-based versions that supposedly could are still work in progress
🔴 Laser beam requires a direct line-of-sight to the target and must maintain contact with the target to burn through its surface – for a ground laser, doing it to a ballistic or a hypersonic missile midflight is a bit problematic
🔴 Laser systems powerful enough to engage targets bigger than a small drone require expensive power and cooling systems
🔴 While conventional air defense system can operate in rainy or cloudy weather, such phenomena degrades the performance of laser weaponry
🔴 Finally, the opposing force can introduce heat-resistant and ablative coatings to help its drones and missiles withstand laser beams
Meanwhile, both Hamas and Hezbollah time and again displayed their ability to bypass Israel’s air defenses and hit Israeli military targets, including radar stations.
Israel’s supposedly sophisticated anti-air weaponry also proved ineffective against massed drone and rocket strikes, proving unable to deal with an overwhelming number of airborne threats, and the new laser systems are yet to display better results.
